newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian pension fund rebuked over housing idea.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian pension fund rebuked over housing idea.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday that the state-run Employees Provident Fund (EPF) should stick to its traditional role of investing workers' pension funds instead of branching out into areas such as running housing boards.

"It is a bit premature for EPF to jump the gun and volunteer new services when I think they should direct themselves to deal with their immediate task," he said when asked to comment on EPF's interest in playing a leading role in meeting the country's low-cost housing needs.
The EPF has about eight million contributors and is one of the country's biggest institutional investors.
Anwar was speaking to reporters after launching a new bond rating agency on Thursday.

EPF executive chairman Sallehuddin Mohamed on Wednesday said the existence of a housing board would make it easier for EPF, with its huge pool of funds, to be involved in the housing industry, especially in building low- and medium-cost houses.
In setting up the board, EPF would be emulating the Singapore Central Provident Fund and its Housing Development Board, Sallehuddin said.
